Command: Do Not Fear Those Who Kill the Body
Summary: Jesus' fear command: do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
Commandment: Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Application: The command reorders fear itself: persecutors have the lesser power. Right fear of God frees disciples from the fear of men.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: to free witnesses from the fear of persecutors by setting the greater judgment of God before them.
Function: Fear needs reordering, and Jesus reorders it here. This one is from the New Testament, not from Moses, so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not apply. Its goal, on the TRADITIONAL reading, was to free witnesses from the fear of persecutors by setting the greater judgment of God before them. The evil it addressed was fear of men — silence bought by the threat of killing the body. It restrained that evil by the greater fear: persecutors have the lesser power, so fear him who can destroy both soul and body.
